svg.title: Suspected Australian snakebite in Victoria: call Triple Zero, keep still and use pressure immobilisation
svg.desc: Working review card for a known or suspected Australian snakebite. Call Triple Zero, keep the person lying still and continuously watched, and start CPR first if the person is unresponsive and not breathing normally. For a known bite site on an arm or leg, the card names one ANZCOR-permitted two-bandage method: a broad elasticised bandage over the bite, then a second broad bandage from just above the fingers or toes upward over clothing, followed by limb immobilisation. The limb picture is a concept map, not wrapping or pressure instruction. Exact pressure, unknown-site care, upper-limb method, no-kit wrapping, self-application and lone-person movement remain withheld pending specialist review and practical testing. Do not wash, cut or suck the bite, use an arterial tourniquet, pursue the snake or remove the bandage before hospital care.
svg.text: Suspected Australian snakebite:
call 000, lie still, keep watching
WARNING — WORKING REVIEW CARD; NOT PRACTICAL TRAINING
Evidence agreement is HIGH for 000, stillness, continuous observation, pressure
immobilisation, CPR priority and the prohibited actions below. It is MODERATE
for reproducing correct pressure and sequence from a static card.
Subjective wording estimates: 95% core actions; 78% selected two-bandage wording.
These are not probabilities of correct pressure, safety, success or survival.
Exact equipment and pressure need toxicology, instructor and practical review. Follow 000.
1 SUSPICION IS ENOUGH — CALL 000 NOW
A bite may be painless and leave no visible mark.
Do not wait for symptoms or for a mark to appear.
Do not remove clothing, search for a bite or try to identify the snake.
Feeling better after an early collapse does not clear the danger.
2 CHECK RESPONSE AND NORMAL BREATHING
UNRESPONSIVE AND NOT BREATHING NORMALLY?
YES — start CPR now. Do not finish bandaging first.
Unresponsive but breathing normally: use the airway/side-position card.
Responsive: have the person lie down and keep completely still.
A second rescuer may bandage only if CPR is not interrupted.
3 CALL, STILLNESS AND WATCHING COME FIRST
• A helper calls while another person gives care, if possible.
• Keep the whole person and bitten limb still. Reassure them.
• Stay beside them and watch response and breathing continuously.
• Bring help and transport to them. Do not let them walk.
Move only the minimum needed for immediate danger or lifesaving care.
4 WHERE IS THE BITE?
LIMB; SITE KNOWN
Use the selected
limb sequence below.
One permitted method;
not proven best.
LIMB; SITE UNKNOWN
Do not search or remove
clothing. Tell 000.
Sequence withheld pending
specialist decision.
NOT ON A LIMB
Do not wrap the head,
neck or chest, or restrict
breathing. Follow 000.
Pressure placement not shown.
5 WITH A KIT — ONE PERMITTED LOCAL-FIRST SEQUENCE
CONCEPT MAP ONLY — it does not show wrap overlap, force or proven pressure.
A KNOWN BITE SITE
Place one broad elasticised
10–15 cm bandage over it.
Do not delay to find an unseen mark.
B WHOLE LIMB
Use a second broad bandage from
just above digits upward, covering
as much limb as possible and the bite.
LOCAL
BANDAGE
WHOLE-LIMB
COVERAGE
SPLINT
DIGITS VISIBLE
C PRESSURE AND SPLINT
• Apply over clothing where practical.
• Keep fingers or toes visible.
• Make the bandage firm and even—
not a narrow arterial tourniquet.
• Splint joints above and below.
• Keep person and limb completely still.
• If the site is already known, mark it
outside and record the times.
A PICTURE CANNOT CHECK
whether pressure is correct.
Exact bandage and pressure need testing.
Upper-limb care needs separate
specialist review.
The shaded limb is a coverage concept, not wrapping geometry or a child-size guide.
6 WITHOUT A PROPER BANDAGE — LOWER-ASSURANCE FALLBACK
Keep the person and limb still. Do not walk away to find equipment.
ANZCOR permits broad clothing or other material; Ambulance Victoria says
a regular bandage or clothing at least 10–15 cm wide may be used.
Do not use a belt, cord, rope, narrow strip or improvised arterial tourniquet.
Exact material, anchoring, overlap, pressure and improvised splint are not illustrated:
each proposed method needs pressure and usability testing first.
7 LEAVE IT IN PLACE. KEEP WATCHING.
• Do not remove, loosen or redo the bandage or splint to inspect the bite.
• Stay with the person. Watch response and normal breathing continuously.
• If breathing becomes abnormal or stops, start CPR immediately.
• Leave removal to the hospital team responsible for treatment.
No field check proves that venom spread has stopped.
DO NOT
✕ wash, cut or suck the bite ✕ apply ice ✕ use an arterial tourniquet
✕ stand or walk ✕ pursue, catch or kill the snake ✕ delay for a photo
✕ remove the bandage before hospital care
PRESSURE IMMOBILISATION ≠ BLEEDING TOURNIQUET
This card is for suspected Australian snakebite—not every bite or sting.
NOT SHOWN: self-application, unknown-site or non-limb technique, upper-limb sling,
child sizing, no-kit wrapping, pressure indicators, or a lone/no-contact walkout rule.
WORKING DRAFT — toxicology, instructor, pressure, practical and stressed-reader review outstanding
